transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Ever since I was there during that shooting on my delivery route, the scene keeps replaying in my head all day and I can’t shut it off. It's just stuck on a loop and I don't know how to make it stop.
How long have you been having these symptoms since the shooting, and have they lasted more than one month?
Everything started immediately after the shooting, which was just about a week ago. It definitely hasn't been a month yet, but it already feels like it's been going on forever.
Since the shooting, have you felt numb, detached, or like the event was unreal or happening in slow motion?
No, I haven't really felt numb or like things weren't real. It's actually the opposite—I feel way too plugged in, constantly on edge and jumpy, and that scene just keeps replaying in my head.
Since the shooting, have you had any moments of feeling confused, in a daze, unable to remember parts of what happened, or like you were watching it from outside your body?

Yes, I actually have some blank spaces in my memory from that night. I remember ducking behind my van and hearing people scream, but there are chunks missing, like how many shots were fired or exactly where the shooter was. No matter how hard I try to replay it, I just can't fill in those gaps.
Since the shooting, have you had any moments where you felt like you were outside your body, in a daze, or like the event was happening again in front of you?

I don't really feel like I'm outside my body, but it definitely feels like the shooting is happening all over again. It's like a loop in my head where I suddenly see the people running past my van and hear the gunshots, and I just freeze up and lose focus completely, whether I'm making a delivery or sitting in church.
Since the shooting, have you been avoiding places, people, conversations, or activities that remind you of it, or trying hard not to think about it?

Yes, I've been doing everything I can to avoid reminders. I make excuses to skip my delivery routes on the Westside, won't go near apartment lots, and even stopped going to my basketball league and choir. If my mom or coworkers try to ask about that night, I shut them down immediately because just talking about it makes my chest tighten up.
Have these symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse since the shooting? Also, have you had nightmares, trouble sleeping, or been extra jumpy since then?

They've been staying constantly bad all week, and my sleep is completely ruined because as soon as I close my eyes I'm back in that parking lot, tossing and turning until I jerk awake at any little noise outside. I'm also incredibly jumpy now—any sudden sound like a car backfires makes my whole body flinch and my heart race like crazy.
Has it been more than a month since the shooting, or are these symptoms still only in the first few weeks after it?
No, it hasn't been a month at all. The shooting happened just about a week ago, so these symptoms have only been going on for this past week.
Have you had any periods of feeling emotionally numb, detached, or like the world around you was unreal since the shooting?
No, I haven't really felt numb or detached, and everything around me feels way too real. It's actually the opposite—I'm constantly anxious, highly on edge, and easily startled by any little thing.
Have you started to feel numb, detached, or emotionally shut down since the shooting, or is it mainly the replaying, fear, and being on edge?

It's definitely the latter, as I don't feel numb or shut down at all; instead, I feel completely overwhelmed and constantly on edge. The shooting just keeps replaying in my head and I jump at every little sound. I'm actively avoiding any reminders of that night because of the intense fear and tension it brings, rather than because I feel detached.
Have your symptoms been present for less than one month since the shooting, or have they continued for more than a month?
They have definitely been present for less than a month. The shooting only happened about a week ago, so I've been dealing with all of this for just this past week.
Has it been less than one month since the shooting, or have these symptoms continued for more than one month?
It has definitely been less than a month since the shooting. It only happened about a week ago, so I've been dealing with all of this for just this past week.
During or right after the shooting, did you feel dazed, unreal, or like you were outside your body, even briefly?
I don't recall feeling dazed, unreal, or outside of my body during the shooting. I was just extremely terrified, though I do have some blank spaces in my memory from that night.
During or right after the shooting, did you feel like time slowed down, you were in a daze, or the event was unreal even for a short time?

I don't really recall feeling like things slowed down or were unreal. It was just extremely chaotic and everything happened so fast while I was trying to hide. I don't think I was in a daze, just incredibly terrified.
During the shooting or right afterward, did you feel dazed, unreal, like time slowed down, or like you were outside your body even briefly?

No, I don't recall feeling like I was outside my body or that time slowed down in that way. I was mostly just terrified and focused on hiding behind my van. I do have some blank spots in my memory about the details of what happened, though.
During the shooting or right afterward, did you feel dazed, unreal, like time slowed down, or like you were outside your body even briefly?

No, I didn't feel like I was outside my body or that time slowed down. Everything was just a huge blur because of how fast it all happened, and I still have some blank spots in my memory from that night.
Just to confirm, did your symptoms start within 4 weeks of the shooting and have you had any dissociative symptoms like feeling detached, unreal, or outside your body at any point since then?

Yes, all of this started just a couple of days after the shooting, so it has only been about a week now. I haven't felt detached, unreal, or outside of my body at any point, though I definitely still have those blank spots in my memory from that night.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed symptoms within days of a qualifying traumatic event (witnessing a shooting), with prominent intrusive re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, and sleep disturbance. However, he explicitly denies the core dissociative symptoms required for acute stress disorder (e.g., feeling detached, unreal, or outside his body), while reporting only memory gaps. Given the very early post-trauma timeframe and the provided candidate set, the best fit is F43.0 (acute stress reaction).
